title: Göbekli Tepe

place.label: Göbekli Tepe, Şanlıurfa Province, Türkiye
place.basis: official UNESCO World Heritage point; not a boundary
place.coords_source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre official point for Göbekli Tepe (World Heritage List 1572), published as N37 13 23.671 E38 55 20.51 at https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1572/maps/ (table read 2026-11-27); approximate, not a boundary

tiers.everyday: Göbekli Tepe in southeast Türkiye is a hilltop with huge carved stone pillars set up by hunter-gatherers around 9600 to 8200 BC, thousands of years before writing or cities.
tiers.student: UNESCO describes monumental enclosures built by hunter-gatherer groups in the Pre-Pottery Neolithic (10th-9th millennia BC), with T-shaped limestone pillars up to 5.5 m tall, some carved as stylised human figures and with wild animals. Pleiades dates the sanctuary to about 9600-8200 BC. It was inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2018.
